name: Chicago Architecture Boat Tour
unique: Ninety minutes up the Chicago River while a docent explains how the city invented the skyscraper, with the river canyon as the classroom.
buzz: The Architecture Center's tour is the one locals recommend; sunset departures are the best. Book ahead in summer.

name: Art Institute of Chicago
unique: Nighthawks, American Gothic, a room of Thorne miniatures and the best Impressionist collection outside Paris, behind a bronze lion on Michigan Avenue.
buzz: The miniatures and the modern wing are the sleeper hits; go on a weekday morning and pick two wings.

name: Second City
unique: The cabaret theater that launched Belushi, Fey and Colbert, still running improvised and scripted shows with a live band and a cheap bar.
buzz: The mainstage shows are consistently sharp; the improv sets are hit or miss and cheaper. Sit close and expect to be teased.

name: Cahokia Mounds
unique: The largest pre-Columbian city north of Mexico, with 120 mounds including Monks Mound — bigger at its base than the Great Pyramid — and a solar calendar of posts.
buzz: The museum is excellent and the climb is easy; sunset from Monks Mound is the move. Quiet and under-visited.

name: Starved Rock
unique: Eighteen sandstone canyons with waterfalls and a lodge on a bluff above the Illinois River, an hour and a half from Chicago.
buzz: The canyons are beautiful and busy; go at 8am and take Trail 2. Bald eagles winter below the dam.

name: Garden of the Gods
unique: Weird sandstone hoodoos, camel-shaped formations and a slot canyon in the Shawnee Hills, with a trail that threads between the rocks.
buzz: People call it a mini-Utah in southern Illinois; it is free and rarely crowded. Combine with the wine trail.

name: Illinois State Fair
unique: A giant state fair with a butter cow, harness racing, a mile-long midway and the Illinois Pork Producers' pork chop on a stick.
buzz: It is the platonic state fair; the butter cow is a genuine attraction. Parking and heat are the usual complaints.
